text:
Bitcoin extended its post-FOMC slide to $64,300–$64,750 during the European session, with the total crypto market cap dropping 3% to $2.2 trillion. Liquidations surged 65% as investors unwound leveraged positions following Chair Kevin Warsh's dot plot revision, which now sees 9 of 18 FOMC members projecting at least one rate hike before year-end.

Institutional positioning remains split. A rare "all-green" session on June 16 saw spot Bitcoin ETFs attract $10.06 million in net inflows led by BlackRock's IBIT at $16.35 million, while ETH, XRP, Solana, and Hyperliquid ETFs also logged inflows — signaling selective risk appetite rather than broad capitulation.

The DXY holding a four-month high near 100.32 remains the decisive macro headwind for digital assets. European benchmarks showed resilience on U.S.-Iran peace optimism, but with the SNB holding at 0% and the Fed projecting further tightening, the dollar's structural strength will continue suppressing BTC's risk premium for institutional allocators.
